definitions: A sacred communal place of the Māori people of New Zealand, typically consisting of a ceremonial ground and a meeting house.
The entire complex of a Māori meeting house, its courtyard, and associated buildings.
examples: The community gathered at the marae for the ceremony.
Visitors are often welcomed onto the marae with a pōwhiri.
Each iwi has its own marae, serving as a focal point for tribal identity.
